newsitem.title: UK: Three groups apply for UK terrestrial digital TV.
newsitem.headline: Three groups apply for UK terrestrial digital TV.

text.p: Three television groups have applied for licences to run Britain's digital terrestrial TV services, the Independent Television Commission watchdog confirmed on Friday.
Two new television companies are bidding for three network licences, or multiplexes, on which no capacity has been set aside for any analogue broadcasters.
Leading heavyweights BSkyB, Carlton Communications and Granada Group, which are teaming up to create a formidable new company -- British Digital Broadcasting.
This other is calling itself Digital Terrestrial Network.

This group is made up of Britain's third largest cable operator CableTel, which is wholly-owned by U.S. cable company International CableTel, and which also owns NTL, one of two major British transmission companies.
These two groups are bidding for multiplexes B, C and D.
Only one company, the digital subsidiary of Welsh Channel Four -- S4C -- has submitted a bid for multiplex A.
Channel 5 and S4C have guaranteed capacity on this network. The winning licence holder is also required to carry Gaelic programmes in Scotland.
Two other licences to operate multiplex services are earmarked for the existing, free, terrestrial broadcasters, the BBC and the ITV commercial network.
Digital television offers more channels, clearer pictures and the possibility of accessing interactive services such as home shopping and home banking.
But with only about 30 channels initially, it had been seen as the poor relation in comparison with BSkyB's planned satellite version, which will offer 200 channels.
The Cable Communications Association says digital cable television will offer up to 1,000 channels.
